preamble: No genuine change of the rhotic /r/ to the open-mid back unrounded vowel [ʌ] has been found. The case previously filed here, non-rhotic African American and Southern US English, is loss of coda /r/: in 'sister' or 'other' the r is dropped and the preceding unstressed vowel surfaces as [ə] (or a lowered [ɐ]). The vowel is not a reflex of the r, so the change is r > ∅ (or r-coloured ɚ > ə), not r > ʌ.

examples.note: Syllable-final r is dropped; the vowel is the unstressed schwa that was already present, not a vocalized [ʌ].

sources: Wikipedia (2026). African-American English (phonology: dropping the r sound at the end of syllables). https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African-American_English
